summary: Iteration 337 — verified INTEGRATION between QC Station (tablet) and Batch Detail per-batch QC flow. Deep-link, inline receive (POST /batches/{id}/move), crates-clamp, submit-through-record_inspection engine, and Inspection Records sync (Resource/Crates/Rejected(btl)/Reason/By) all work end-to-end. Wrote 4 new backend integration tests (all pass) and re-ran 18 existing QC-Station + Live-Board regression tests (all pass). UI verified: QC Station header button on Batch Detail, deep link opens the batch's stage step, crates input clamps to stage.pending, standalone QC Station and QC Live Board still function.
critical_code_review_comments: QCStation.saveCrates() clamps to pendingFor(batch, stage) client-side and shows a warning toast — good. However, if a user opens two capture sessions in different tabs, both could set crates_inspected = pending and submit sequentially; the server-side guard 'Only N crates pending' correctly rejects the second submit (verified via 400) so integrity is preserved.

receiveCrates() and Batch Detail's handleMove() both hit POST /batches/{id}/move so behaviour is consistent — same endpoint, same balances (verified: unallocated decreased, received+pending increased by qty).
InspectionRecordsTable renders both new (entries[]) and legacy (flat) inspection shapes — good backwards compatibility.

Minor UX: after 'Received via QC Station', the Rejections rejected-cost panel on Batch Detail may still show 'Some rejections have no cost mapping configured' if the mapping for reason x stage is missing. Not new — same behaviour as manual inspect. Not a blocker.

QCStation.js is 432 lines with a single default export handling batch/stage/capture in one component using local step state — acceptable for the current UX. If a 4th step is added, extract into three subcomponents to keep it under 500 lines.

Session-submit uses record_inspection under the hood which respects total_rej_bottles <= qty_inspected * bottles_per_crate. On the tablet, if operator taps way more bottles than can fit given crates chosen, submit will 400. Consider surfacing this preemptively in the capture screen (disable submit or show hint) — polish only.
